MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Infrastructure Engineering | CI/CD, Kubernetes & Terraform
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines and ephemeral test environments used by three product teams. Hands-on experience with Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, complemented by a personal k3s and GitOps homelab and Terraform infrastructure work. Experienced in improving pipeline performance, documenting technical processes and bringing teams along with infrastructure changes.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Terraform, Argo CD
Containers & Systems: Kubernetes (namespace-level work), k3s, Linux, Ansible (basic)
Monitoring & Data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Programming & Automation: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Cloud learning: AWS basics (EC2, S3; personal learning)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Profiled and improved pipelines by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end testing; reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Built merge-request ephemeral environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster. Each environment includes the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and is automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built test-result collection and Grafana dashboards to identify flaky tests by team.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling for PostgreSQL test-data seeding and authored an internal guide to CI used in team onboarding.
- Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated approaches.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, reproducing bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Set up a three-node k3s cluster on Raspberry Pi 5 devices, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Configured Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented short-lived application and PostgreSQL environments deployed via Helm to the shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI.
- Enabled QA and product reviewers to assess changes before merge, with end-to-end tests running against each environment.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Improved pipelines across three teams through test-job parallelisation, dependency caching and a separate end-to-end stage.
- Reduced average pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Preparing for Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA); exam scheduled for January 2027.
Terraform Associate practice tests completed; certification exam not taken.

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
Mentored two QA interns in 2023.

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, quantified, and professionally written. It presents a credible QA-to-DevOps transition with strong evidence in CI/CD, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes usage, monitoring, and pipeline optimisation. The strongest achievements are specific and measurable: pipeline duration reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, and flaky tests reduced from 7% to below 1%. The main content limitation is that the document can appear stronger than the candidate's actual infrastructure scope unless its boundaries remain explicit: Kubernetes work is namespace-level, Terraform is primarily personal-project experience, and there is no production cloud ownership or on-call experience shown. The CV also gives limited evidence of systems architecture, networking, security, or stakeholder leadership beyond CI and test infrastructure.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological experience, plain text formatting, and searchable technology keywords. It should parse well in most ATS platforms. Relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, and Argo CD are present. AI screening may identify a credible junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-engineering profile, but may rank the CV below candidates with stronger Terraform/Terragrunt, AWS, networking, security, and production infrastructure experience. The headline 'DevOps / Infrastructure Engineering' is attention-grabbing but should be supported by clearer scope language so it does not imply ownership of cluster operations or broad cloud production infrastructure. Git, GitLab API, cert-manager, and pytest-xdist are supported by the original material but are absent or inconsistently represented in the document.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a partial but truthful match. It demonstrates hands-on infrastructure-related engineering through GitLab CI ownership, Docker and Helm deployments, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, monitoring, Linux, Terraform-based personal infrastructure, and analytical optimisation. It also shows ownership of a technical topic and communication through pipeline ownership, the internal CI onboarding guide, mentoring, and enabling QA/product reviewers. AWS basics are accurately disclosed as learning experience, and Java test automation provides limited JVM-adjacent background. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps in strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud environment ownership, systems architecture/system design, mTLS, broader networking, practical security, IoT or remote-device integration, and virtual machines. These are job-alignment gaps rather than document defects. The role appears to expect a more experienced infrastructure engineer who can design and operate secure train-to-cloud systems from the start, while this CV currently supports a junior-to-mid DevOps/platform transition profile.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL ISSUES: None identified. The CV's technologies and experience are supported by the Original Candidate Information, and it correctly discloses namespace-level Kubernetes work, AWS learning status, and uncompleted certifications.

MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the infrastructure scope more precise while preserving the strongest match. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2 years owning CI/CD and test infrastructure for three product teams. Hands-on with GitLab CI, Docker, Helm and namespace-level Kubernetes deployments, plus personal Terraform-based infrastructure and a k3s GitOps homelab." This is more directly aligned with the ad and avoids implying cluster-administration or broad production-cloud ownership.

2. In the Professional Summary or the Odrava Health experience section, make the stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence explicit using existing facts. Add a sentence or bullet such as: "Authored the internal CI guide used in team onboarding and enabled QA and product reviewers to validate changes in ephemeral environments." This better supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along without overstating formal leadership.

3. In the Technical Skills section, add supported keywords currently missing from the document: "Git, GitLab API, cert-manager, pytest-xdist." Place Git under Infrastructure & CI/CD or Tools, cert-manager under Containers & Systems or Security/TLS, and GitLab API and pytest-xdist under Programming & Automation or Testing. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, or production AWS experience because the original information does not support them.

4. In the Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps project, clarify the exact Terraform scope and distinguish it from professional cloud infrastructure. Change "Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform" to "Provisioned infrastructure for a small personal Hetzner VPS with Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level." This maintains credibility and prevents ATS or recruiter interpretation that Terraform was used extensively in production.

5. In the Odrava Health experience section, strengthen the infrastructure-operation keywords with the existing technical facts. Revise the Kubernetes bullet to: "Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; create Helm deployments for ephemeral test environments, while the platform team operates the cluster." This is more precise and matches the job's infrastructure-operation terminology without claiming cluster ownership.

6. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, retain the transparent status wording but make it more ATS-readable: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — exam scheduled January 2027; not yet certified" and "Terraform Associate — practice tests completed; certification not taken." This prevents either item from being misread as a completed certification.

7. In the Technical Skills section, separate learning-level cloud exposure from professional experience more clearly. Change "Cloud learning: AWS basics (EC2, S3; personal learning)" to "Cloud: AWS basics (EC2, S3) — personal learning; no professional AWS experience." This is already truthful in substance and makes the limitation immediately clear to human and AI reviewers.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, readable, professional, and substantially stronger than a generic QA CV for a DevOps transition. It uses clear section headings, strong quantified achievements, relevant project evidence, and accurate scope clarification around shared Kubernetes access. The strongest content includes the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, ephemeral environments, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The main content limitation is that several capabilities relevant to this role are either only implied or are not supported by the candidate's background: systems architecture, networking, security, production operations, and cloud design. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects. The CV also gives considerable space to QA testing tools, which may dilute the infrastructure-engineering positioning for this specific role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is good. The document uses conventional headings, plain text formatting, standard date and job-title structures, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, graphics, columns, or parsing obstacles. Relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Linux, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, and infrastructure are present. AI screening probability is moderate to good for infrastructure-transition roles, but likely lower for this particular vacancy because the CV does not contain Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, security, networking, or strong AWS experience. The explicit qualifiers such as "namespace-level work," "AWS basics," and "personal learning" are valuable because they prevent overstatement, although they also accurately signal limited depth in some required areas.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, containerized test environments, Kubernetes deployment at namespace level, infrastructure automation, observability, analytical improvement, documentation, and technical ownership. It also reflects Corvale's ownership and collaborative culture through ownership of pipelines for three teams, onboarding documentation, mentoring, and enabling QA and product reviewers. However, the candidate's material shows important gaps for this contractor role: no Terragrunt, no demonstrated mTLS, no demonstrated production cloud ownership, no production on-call ownership, no explicit practical security work, and no IoT, automotive, train, or remote-device integration. Terraform is demonstrated through a personal Hetzner project rather than substantial professional cloud infrastructure. AWS is only at a basic learning level. The candidate has Java test-code experience, but not the backend/JVM background described as a nice-to-have. The CV is therefore a credible transition profile, but not yet a strong match for a role requiring independent cloud architecture and secure train-to-cloud infrastructure from the start.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the transition and infrastructure scope even more explicit without implying production platform ownership. For example, change the opening to: "QA automation engineer transitioning into DevOps and platform engineering, with 7 years of experience and the last two focused primarily on CI/CD, ephemeral environments, Kubernetes deployments, and build tooling." Retain the accurate statement that the platform team operates the shared cluster.
2. In the Technical Skills section, separate professional experience from personal learning more clearly. Use labels such as "Professional: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes namespace-level deployments, Python, Bash, Linux, PostgreSQL, Prometheus/Grafana dashboards" and "Personal projects: Terraform, k3s, Argo CD, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, Ansible, AWS basics, Hetzner." This makes the CV more credible for ATS and human reviewers and prevents personal-project tools from appearing equivalent to production experience.
3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, add the existing stakeholder and technical-leadership evidence to a bullet rather than leaving it only in the summary. For example: "Authored the internal CI guide used in team onboarding and coordinated adoption of pipeline and ephemeral-environment changes across three product teams (~25 developers)." This directly supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along.
4. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under "Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps," clarify the exact TLS evidence without overstating networking expertise. Change the monitoring/TLS bullet to: "Configured Traefik ingress and cert-manager for TLS certificate management; deployed Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring." Do not add mTLS, network design, firewalling, or security claims because they are not supported by the original candidate information.
5. In the Skills section, avoid presenting Terraform as strong professional experience. Change "Infrastructure & CI/CD: ... Terraform, Argo CD" to a structure that identifies Terraform as personal-project experience, and in the project entry retain the concrete evidence: "Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS with Terraform." This is more truthful and better aligned with the actual evidence.
6. In the Certifications & Professional Development section, retain the clear status wording but make it more ATS-readable: "Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) — preparation in progress; exam scheduled January 2027 (not yet certified)" and "Terraform Associate — practice tests completed; certification not taken." Do not describe either as a certification.

MINOR ENHANCEMENTS:
7. In the Technical Skills section, move "Linux" into a dedicated "Systems" or "Operating Systems" category rather than grouping it only with containers. This makes the Linux requirement easier for ATS and recruiters to identify.
8. In the Odrava Health experience bullets, change "Work with namespace-level access on the shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster" to "Deploy and support Helm-based test environments with namespace-level access on a shared Kubernetes cluster; the platform team operates the cluster." This leads with the candidate's actual contribution while preserving the important scope limitation.
9. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section, retain the Flaky Test Dashboard as a project or integrate its evidence into Odrava experience, because it demonstrates analytical thinking, observability, PostgreSQL, Python, Grafana, and measurable operational improvement. If space is limited, replace the duplicated "CI Pipeline Speed-up" project with the Flaky Test Dashboard project rather than repeating the same 38-to-14-minute achievement twice.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, truthful, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into DevOps and platform engineering. The Professional Summary accurately explains the candidate's scope, including the important distinction between deploying to a shared Kubernetes cluster and operating the cluster itself. The experience bullets use measurable outcomes effectively: pipeline time reduced from 38 to 14 minutes, runner costs reduced by about 30%, and flaky tests reduced to below 2%. The selected infrastructure projects add useful evidence of Terraform, GitOps, observability, ingress, and TLS-related work. The main content limitation is that systems architecture, stakeholder leadership, and security-related experience are not expressed as explicitly as the target role requires. The CV also appropriately discloses that the CKA and Terraform Associate certifications have not been obtained.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly parseable: it uses conventional headings, plain text contact details, standard employment entries, and clearly separated skills and projects. Relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Python, Bash, Linux, AWS, Argo CD, Grafana, PostgreSQL, and TLS are present. The 'Personal projects' skills label and the certification status wording are ATS-safe and help distinguish professional experience from learning. No formatting or potential hallucination issue was detected.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's hands-on infrastructure direction through GitLab CI ownership, Docker and Helm deployments, namespace-level Kubernetes work, ephemeral environments, Terraform on Hetzner, and a k3s/GitOps homelab. It also demonstrates ownership, analytical thinking, measurable improvement, documentation, and collaboration across three product teams. AWS is represented accurately as personal learning rather than professional cloud experience. The strongest gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, mTLS, broader networking and security, production cloud infrastructure operation, and IoT or remote-device integration. The candidate's material also does not establish backend or full-stack experience beyond Java test code. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved by wording. The CV does contain adjacent evidence for system design and technical leadership, but it should make that evidence more visible for this role. The ownership and engineering-led culture signals are a reasonable fit, especially through owning shared CI infrastructure, enabling QA and product reviewers, and documenting processes used in onboarding.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, truthful and well-structured CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It uses clear section headings, reverse-chronological experience, quantified outcomes, relevant infrastructure projects and transparent certification status. The strongest evidence is the ownership of GitLab CI for three teams, the reduction of pipeline duration from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% runner-cost reduction, the ephemeral Kubernetes environments and the homelab infrastructure work. The main content weakness is repetition: the Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments project substantially repeats the Odrava experience bullets. The CV also presents the candidate's strongest transferable evidence, such as stakeholder enablement and infrastructure-as-code exposure, but does not frame it as explicitly as the target role does.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The document is highly ATS-compatible: it uses standard headings, plain text formatting, conventional dates, readable job titles and searchable technology names. Relevant terms include GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Linux, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python, Bash, TLS and Argo CD. The AI screening probability is moderate for this specific vacancy: the CV should be recognized as a DevOps/infrastructure transition profile, but screening may be reduced by the absence of Terragrunt, mTLS, system design, security and professional AWS/cloud-operation evidence. Those are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be added without supporting evidence. Repeating the same ephemeral-environment project in both Experience and Selected Infrastructure Projects may also dilute keyword relevance slightly, although it does not create a parsing problem.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the role's infrastructure-engineering, CI/CD, Kubernetes, Linux, analytical-thinking and communication themes. It also provides credible evidence of ownership and stakeholder enablement: the candidate owns pipelines for three product teams, authored an internal CI guide and helped teams adopt changes. The homelab demonstrates Terraform, GitOps, monitoring, ingress and certificate-management exposure. However, the target role expects production-oriented cloud infrastructure design and operation, strong Terraform and Terragrunt, system architecture, mTLS/network design, practical security awareness and technical leadership across external stakeholders. The candidate's material shows no Terragrunt, no mTLS, no professional AWS/cloud operation, no IoT or remote-device integration, no virtual-machine experience and no backend/full-stack development beyond Java test code. The CV appropriately avoids claiming these capabilities. Company-culture alignment is indirect but credible through ownership, collaboration across three teams, documentation and improvement of shared engineering workflows.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, professional, readable, and strongly evidence-based. It presents measurable outcomes, relevant project detail, ownership, and a credible QA-to-DevOps transition. The distinction between professional Kubernetes access and personal infrastructure work is especially valuable and prevents overstating cluster administration experience. The main content issue is repetition between the Professional Summary, current-role bullets, and Selected Infrastructure Projects. The summary is also somewhat dense and includes one unsupported implication about documentation adoption. Overall, the document is convincing for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform-engineering profile, though it does not establish senior cloud-infrastructure depth.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain-text contact details, and standard skill categories should parse well in most ATS systems. Relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, Python, Bash, Linux, Grafana, PostgreSQL, AWS, and infrastructure as code are present. The CV should have a good ATS and AI-screening probability for DevOps, CI/CD, Kubernetes, and test-infrastructure roles. Matching probability for this specific role will be lower because Terragrunt, mTLS, systems architecture, security awareness, and cloud operation are either absent or not explicitly evidenced. The current wording is generally ATS-safe; avoid introducing unsupported keywords merely to match the advertisement.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with hands-on infrastructure engineering for CI/CD and ephemeral environments, analytical problem-solving, Linux, observability, Kubernetes deployments, Terraform practice, and technical documentation. The candidate also demonstrates ownership across three product teams and stakeholder value through environments used by QA and product reviewers. AWS is present only as personal learning, which is a partial match to the preferred requirement. The principal gaps are strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud environment design and operation, mTLS, broader networking, explicit practical security work, IoT or remote-device integration, and backend or full-stack experience. The CV shows useful adjacent evidence for systems design through the ephemeral-environment workflow and for TLS through cert-manager, but it does not demonstrate the full depth requested for a contractor shaping train-to-cloud infrastructure from the start. The QA-to-DevOps transition and lack of production on-call experience also make the profile better aligned with a junior-to-mid infrastructure role than with a fully independent contractor expected to lead production architecture.
